description.narrative: The Project development objective is to improve integrated urban management, service delivery, and disaster emergency management in Western Area and secondary cities of Sierra Leone.

The Project is designed to support an integrated urban resilience intervention that takes a spatial approach to address in a comprehensive manner the multi-sectoral urban development challenges of the country, including urban governance, service delivery and disaster risk management. The Project is structured into four components. Component 1: Institutional and Capacity Development in Integrated Urban Management; Component 2: Resilient Municipal Infrastructure Investment and Urban Greening; Component 3: Emergency Management Institutional and Capacity Development; Component 4: Project Management.

condition.narrative: Per the ESCP, the Recipient shall prepare a GBV Action Plan during the first quarter of implementation and approved not later thanninety days of the Effective Date, which will then form part of the Contractors' ESMP.
Per the ESCP, the Recipient shall, not later than sixty days of the Effective Date, prepare a COVID-19 Prevention and RiskManagement Plan, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.
Per the ESCP, the Recipient shall, not later than thirty days of the Effective Date, hire an NGO to support the GBV Action Planimplementation, including designing the GBV-related GRM.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.2(a): The Recipient shall, at all times during implementation of the Project, maintain the ProjectManagement Unit (PMU) under the FDD with terms of reference, resources and technical staff, satisfactory to the Association,including a Project manager, a financial management specialist or an accountant, a procurement specialist, a civil engineer, amonitoring and evaluation specialist, an environmental specialist, a social specialist, a gender, and gender-based violencespecialist, and a communications and community engagement specialist, all with terms of reference, qualifications, and experience,satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.2(c): The Recipient shall, at all times during the Project implementation, maintain the PFMU within the MoFwith terms of reference, resources and technical staff, satisfactory to the Association. The PFMU shall be responsible for managingthe fiduciary (i.e., financial management and procurement) aspects of the Project.
Schedule 2, Section I.A.3(a): The Recipient shall maintain the Project Steering Committee throughout the Project implementationperiod.
Schedule 2, Section I.A.4(a): The Recipient shall maintain the Project Technical Committee throughout the Project implementationperiod.

Schedule 2, Section I.E: The Recipient shall, not later than sixty (60) days of the Effective Date, establish, operationalize, andthereafter, maintain throughout Project implementation, a grievance mechanism, in form and substance satisfactory to theAssociation.

comment.narrative: The neighborhood upgrading works have not commenced. Designs for both interventions are currently at final stages. Over 80,000 residents in the three neighbourhoods targeted for upgrading in Rokupa, Coconut Farm, and Moyiba, are expected to benefit from improved access to sanitation and portable water upon the completion of works. It is expected that procurement of construction works will commence before May 2025.

comment.narrative: The project has equipped NDMA headquarters and regional offices. Over 400 staff and volunteers have been trained on the delivery of emergency support functions. The EOC is expected to be completed as planned, following progress in resolving the land availability issues.

title.narrative: Proportion of safely disposed municipal solid waste in Western Area

comment.narrative: The sanitary landfill construction will be cancelled following the proposed restructuring, the design and associated ESF contracts under preparation have been closed. Relevant indicators linked to the sanitary landfill will be deleted.

The three settlements targeted for upgrading, including Moyiba, Coconut Farm and Rokupa, accommodate over 80,000 residents on approximately 206 hectares. The design and feasibility and safeguards studies are ongoing. It is expected that construction works will commence before May 2025. This indicator will be revised to unbundle urban upgrading interventions.

title.narrative: City councils with ICT system for property tax upgraded/established and operational

comment.narrative: This activity will support 6 City Councils and 1 district council in the establishment of web-based property tax systems. The procurement of Phase one activities including the Assessment of the Municipal Finance Capacity in Secondary cities and WARDC and piloting in one council , is at advanced stages of procurement with the consultant expected to commence in January 2025. In parallel, the Fiscal Decentralization Division (FDD) will continue to support local councils in establishing institutional structures as the District Local Revenue Mobilization Committees, and in the development of a revenue mobilization strategy for City Councils.

title.narrative: Cities with new planning frameworks adopted

comment.narrative:
While the actual results to date remains zero, achievement of the target is on track, and will likely be exceeded. The consultancy for the preparation of the Western Area Rural Development Council (WARDC) Development Plan has been adopted in Oct 2024 and will be launched in Feb 2025. The Western Area Spatial Plan and 6 spatial plans for secondary city local councils is to be completed in May 2025.
In parallel the project is providing support to the review and update of the Town and Country Planning Act, which when adopted will strengthen cities ability to enforce these plans, supported by regulations.

title.narrative: Staff trained in urban planning methods

comment.narrative: The project has trained over 100 staff in urban planning to date, however there are still significant capacity gaps at the municipality and local council level. The target will be increased to accommodate more training based on the proposed restructuring.

title.narrative: Increased municipal own source revenue (aggregated for all city councils)

comment.narrative: The project has provided technical support to all secondary cities in terms of computers and mobility which has contributed to increased own source revenue mobilization. In addition, capacity support has also been provided to the Fiscal Decentralization Department (FDD) in the Ministry of Finance, which supports local councils, such as the District Local Revenue Mobilization Committees. It must also be noted that the big increase in 28% by end of 2022 since the baseline in 2020 can partially be explained by revenue mobilization rates decreasing during COVID. Looking forward, the project will develop of a revenue mobilization strategy for City Councils and upgrade property tax system in 6 City Councils and 1 district council in the establishment of web-based property tax systems, for which Phase one activities, including the assessment of the Municipal Finance Capacity in Secondary cities and WARDC and piloting in one council is just starting.

title.narrative: People provided with access to enhanced hydromet early warning systems

comment.narrative: The Project has been supporting extensive technical assistance around the development of hydromet early warning systems in SL to inform the technical specifications and operational procedures for the new system. Additionally, the project is supporting NWRMA and SLMet to rehabilitate their non-functional stations rehabilitate new ones where they are required, with the procurement process for the purchase of equipment is at advanced stages. It is expected that the system will be fully operational by early 2025. Further sensitization of communities on early warning systems will be undertaken.

The assumption is that growing to maturity of 1 million trees will lead to the reduction of 76,000 tonnes of GHG. This would be fully achieved by 2026.
The deferment of the landfill construction will reduce GHG emission reduction targets considerably, so this target will need to be revised downwards.
